en: Arjuna said: Strong-armed Hrishikesha, slayer of Keshi, I wish to know the true meaning of renunciation (sannyasa) and of letting go (tyaga), each one separately.

first: काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः ।
en: Krishna said: The wise understand renunciation as giving up actions done out of desire. The thoughtful call giving up the fruits of all actions letting go.
Some thinkers say that action should be given up as faulty. Others say that acts of sacrifice, giving and austerity should not be given up.

first: निश्चयं शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम ।
en: Hear my firm view on letting go, best of the Bharatas. Letting go, tiger among men, is said to be of three kinds.
Acts of sacrifice, giving and austerity should not be given up; they should be done. Sacrifice, giving and austerity purify the wise.

first: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च ।
en: But even these actions should be done giving up attachment and the wish for fruits. This, Partha, is my firm and highest view.
Giving up a duty that one is meant to do is not right. Abandoning it out of confusion is called tamasic.
If a person gives up an action because it is painful, out of fear of bodily trouble, that letting go is rajasic, and they do not gain its fruit.
When a duty is done only because it ought to be done, Arjuna, giving up attachment and its fruit, that letting go is held to be sattvic.
One who truly lets go, filled with sattva, wise and free of doubt, does not hate unpleasant work and does not cling to pleasant work.

first: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः ।
en: An embodied being cannot give up action completely. But whoever gives up the fruits of action is called one who truly lets go.

first: अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम् ।
en: For those who have not let go, the fruit of action after death is of three kinds: unwanted, wanted and mixed. But for those who have renounced, there is none at all.
Strong-armed one, learn from me the five causes for the completion of every action, as taught in the Sankhya teaching.

first: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् ।
en: The body as the base, the doer, the various instruments, the many different kinds of effort, and fifth, fate (the divine).
Whatever action a person begins with body, speech or mind, right or wrong, these five are its causes.

first: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः ।
en: This being so, whoever sees themselves alone as the doer, because their understanding is not trained, does not see; their mind is clouded.

first: यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते ।
en: One who has no sense of 'I am the doer' and whose understanding is not stained, even if they kill these people, does not kill and is not bound.
Knowledge, the object known and the knower are the three things that move one to act. The instrument, the action and the doer are the three parts of action.

first: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः ।
en: Knowledge, action and the doer are said in the teaching of the gunas to be of three kinds, according to the gunas. Hear about them as they are.
The knowledge by which one sees one undying reality in all beings, undivided among the divided, know that to be sattvic.
The knowledge that sees in all beings many separate realities of different kinds, know that to be rajasic.
The knowledge that clings to one small thing as if it were everything, without reason, without grasp of the truth and narrow, is called tamasic.
Action that is required, done without attachment, without liking or dislike, by one who does not want its fruit, is called sattvic.

first: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहंकारेण वा पुनः ।
en: Action done with great strain by one seeking to satisfy desires, or full of ego, is called rajasic.
Action begun out of confusion, without thinking of the results, the loss, the harm to others or one's own ability, is called tamasic.
A doer who is free from attachment, does not boast, is full of firmness and enthusiasm, and is unchanged by success or failure is called sattvic.
A doer who is full of passion, wants the fruits of action, is greedy, harmful, impure, and swings between joy and grief is called rajasic.
A doer who is undisciplined, crude, stubborn, deceitful, spiteful, lazy, gloomy and slow to act is called tamasic.
Now hear, Dhananjaya, the threefold division of understanding and of firmness according to the gunas, explained fully and one by one.

first: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये ।
en: The understanding that knows when to act and when to hold back, what should and should not be done, what to fear and what not to fear, and what binds and what frees, is sattvic, Partha.

first: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च ।
en: The understanding by which one knows wrongly what is right and wrong, and what should and should not be done, is rajasic, Partha.
The understanding that, covered by darkness, takes wrong to be right and sees everything upside down is tamasic, Partha.
The steady firmness by which, through yoga, one holds the workings of the mind, the breath and the senses is sattvic, Partha.
The firmness by which one holds on to duty, pleasure and wealth, wanting their fruits out of attachment, is rajasic, Partha.

first: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च ।
en: The firmness by which a foolish person does not let go of sleep, fear, grief, gloom and pride is tamasic, Partha.

first: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ ।
en: Now hear from me, best of the Bharatas, about the three kinds of happiness: the happiness one comes to enjoy through practice and in which pain comes to an end.
That which is like poison at first but like nectar in the end, born of a clear understanding of the Self, is called sattvic happiness.
That which comes from the contact of the senses with their objects, like nectar at first but like poison in the end, is called rajasic happiness.
The happiness that confuses the self from start to finish and comes from sleep, laziness and carelessness is called tamasic.

first: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः ।
en: There is no being on earth, or in heaven among the gods, that is free from these three gunas born of nature.
The duties of Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras are divided, Parantapa, according to the gunas arising from their own nature.
Calm, self-control, austerity, purity, patience, honesty, knowledge, wisdom and faith are the natural duties of a Brahmin.
Courage, vigour, firmness, skill, not running from battle, generosity and leadership are the natural duties of a Kshatriya.
Farming, caring for cattle and trade are the natural duties of a Vaishya. Work of service is the natural duty of a Shudra.

first: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः ।
en: Each person, devoted to their own work, reaches perfection. Hear how one devoted to their own work finds perfection.
By worshipping through one's own work the One from whom all beings come and by whom all this is filled, a person finds perfection.
Better is one's own duty, even done imperfectly, than another's duty done well. Doing the work that suits one's nature, one does not commit sin.

first: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् ।
en: Kaunteya, one should not give up the work one is born to, even if it has faults. For every undertaking is covered by faults, as fire is covered by smoke.
One whose understanding is unattached everywhere, who has mastered the self and is free from craving, reaches through renunciation the highest perfection of freedom from action.

first: सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे ।
en: Learn from me in brief, Kaunteya, how one who has reached perfection reaches Brahman, the highest goal of knowledge.

first: बुद्ध्या विशुद्ध्या युक्तो धृत्यात्मानं नियम्य च ।
en: With a pure understanding, controlling oneself with firmness, turning away from sound and other sense objects, and setting aside liking and dislike;
living in a quiet place, eating lightly, controlling speech, body and mind, always devoted to meditation, and relying on detachment;

first: अहंकारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् ।
en: letting go of ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessions, free from the sense of 'mine' and at peace, one becomes fit to be one with Brahman.

first: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।
en: Having become one with Brahman, calm within, one neither grieves nor craves. The same toward all beings, one gains the highest devotion to me.
Through devotion one comes to know me truly, how great I am and who I am. Then, knowing me truly, one enters into me at once.
Even while always doing all kinds of work, one who takes refuge in me reaches by my grace the eternal, undying home.
In your mind give all your actions to me, hold me as the highest, rely on the yoga of understanding, and keep your mind always on me.
With your mind on me, you will cross all difficulties by my grace. But if out of ego you do not listen, you will be lost.
If, relying on your ego, you think 'I will not fight', your decision is false. Your own nature will make you fight.
Kaunteya, bound by your own work born of your nature, what you do not wish to do out of confusion you will do anyway, against your will.
The Lord lives in the heart of all beings, Arjuna, turning them all around by his power, as if they were mounted on a machine.
Take refuge in him alone with your whole being, Bharata. By his grace you will gain the highest peace and the eternal home.
So I have given you knowledge more secret than any secret. Think it over fully, and then do as you wish.

first: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
en: Hear once more my highest word, the most secret of all. You are deeply loved by me, so I will tell you what is good for you.

first: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।
en: Keep your mind on me, be devoted to me, worship me, bow to me. You will surely come to me. I promise you truly, for you are dear to me.
Let go of all duties and take refuge in me alone. I will free you from all sins; do not grieve.
This should never be told to one without self-discipline, without devotion, without the wish to listen, or to one who finds fault with me.
Whoever shares this highest secret with my devotees, having shown the highest devotion to me, will surely come to me.
No one among humans does more pleasing service to me than such a person, and no one on earth will be dearer to me.

first: अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः ।
en: And whoever studies this sacred conversation of ours worships me through the sacrifice of knowledge. That is my view.
Even a person who only listens to it, with faith and without finding fault, will be freed and reach the happy worlds of those whose deeds are good.
Partha, have you heard this with a focused mind? Dhananjaya, has your confusion born of ignorance been destroyed?
Arjuna said: My confusion is gone, and by your grace, Achyuta, I have my memory back. I stand firm, free of doubt. I will do as you say.
Sanjaya said: So I heard this wonderful conversation between Vasudeva and the great-souled Partha, and it made my hair stand on end.
By the grace of Vyasa I heard this highest secret yoga directly from Krishna, the master of yoga, as he himself spoke it.
O King, as I remember again and again this wonderful and holy conversation between Keshava and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.
And as I remember again and again that most wonderful form of Hari, my amazement is great, O King, and I rejoice again and again.

first: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः ।
en: Wherever there is Krishna, the master of yoga, and wherever there is Partha, the archer, there will surely be fortune, victory, wealth and right conduct. That is my belief.
